overclaims: The underlying paper identifies product brainstorming, press-release drafts and persuasive memos among the tasks.
The randomized GPT-4 experiment found benefits on tasks including ideation and writing, but worse correctness on a managerial task outside its capabilities.
This supports usefulness with human checking.
checks.note: Excerpt and locator are fine, and the outcome matches the reviews. The visible evidence never says the brainstorming or drafting tasks fell inside the frontier. It never names product brainstorming, press releases, memos or a managerial task. Table 2 isn't shown, and e2's 'creative, analytical, and writing' fragment describes earlier AI work, not this study's results. So the rationale's 'improved work involving ideas and drafts' isn't supported. 'Usefulness with human checking' clashes with e2: AI degraded performance even with humans in the loop.
